text: The other lads' account of Monday evening and the night
why: The two other lads are introduced as having supper at the trainer's house that Monday evening, so their account is a natural item.

text: Edith Baxter's account: the supper, the stranger, the window, the cravat
why: No stranger, window or cravat has appeared yet; the story only shows the maid carrying the supper.

text: Ned Hunter's account: the window, the dog, the search, the message, the drugging
why: The window, a dog, a search, a message and a drugging have not been mentioned yet.
Two of the lads walked up to the trainer's house for supper.
The path across the open moor is mentioned.
Hunter's supper was a dish of curried mutton.
This is a plain paraphrase of the supper carried down to Hunter.
There was a water-tap in the stables.
The stables were locked up at nine, which implies a door.

text: The kitchen of the trainer's house
why: The lads had supper in the kitchen of the trainer's house.
The stables were locked at nine o'clock on Monday night.
The maid set out at a few minutes after nine.
No stranger has been introduced, let alone one who stops the maid.
A stable window has not been mentioned; this anticipates later events.

text: Hunter goes for the dog; the maid flees
why: Neither a dog nor the maid fleeing has appeared in the story.
